utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, everybody. Mr. Lukic, do you have any questions -- or Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Trisic. Mr. Lukic informed me about yesterday's examination, and today in talking with our client -- after talking to our client, I can say that we have no questions for this particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much and welcome back to this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey, any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, everyone, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Trisic. Mr. Trisic, can you tell us how well you know Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in terms of time, I've known him for two years. And I knew him before also, but we really just only occasionally met. We were not -- it was not as if we met regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's from Bratunac; you're from Bratunac. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say those two years, was that the two years that you were working under him from -- during the war years?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us, what kind of commander was he? Was he a good commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he respected by his troops and by his officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was held in high esteem, exceptionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the kind of man you could come to when you needed to? Was his door always open?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly the way it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did he communicate well with his officers and his troops?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he didn't secret himself off and he wasn't a loner?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. He wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he issue clear and concise orders to his men and his officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday I heard a general in another matter being interviewed, and the person asked him: How can you be responsible for a thousand men under your command? And the general said: The chain of command is an extension of me. Do you agree with that? In the VRS, is the chain of command under a commander an extension of that commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is a fact of life in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's more than just a fact of life; it's a fundamental principle, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Colonel Blagojevic the kind of man that would take responsibility for the problems that arose and the things that occurred, or was he the kind of guy that would blame others; blame his subordinates or blame his superiors?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was rather the kind of guy who would take responsibility up on his shoulders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And a sign of a critical part of command is keeping well-informed of what's going on around you, isn't it? Lives depend on it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the way it ought to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's a critical part of command, isn't it, keeping informed? A good commander keeps informed of what's going on around him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Colonel Blagojevic was a good commander.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when there are senior officers about in the brigade area, from the corps, from the Main Staff, that's potentially problematic for yourself and for your commander, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If those officers - for example, General Krstic or General Mladic - issue orders, it's -- would be the brigade commander's responsibility to carry out any orders issued to him or his officers, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would be natural for a commander in the situation of Commander Blagojevic to try to keep track of what Mladic and General Krstic had in mind, what their orders were, what they wanted, in order not to get himself in trouble with them and undercut their plans.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nobody would want to undercut General Mladic, because if you did, your career could go down the drain, couldn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you a document, if I could. It's a document -- I think it's dated 1993, October. It's P857/A. And this document -- just near the end, if you could take a look at it, it just makes a reference that Lieutenant Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic was appointed to that position, meaning the chief of staff of the -- looks like the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. Do you remember a time in late 1993 when Colonel Blagojevic was the chief of staff of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you -- I apologise. Would you be so kind as to repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. Do you remember a time in late 1993 when Colonel Blagojevic - or I guess at this time he was a lieutenant colonel - was appointed to the position of chief of staff of the Bratunac Brigade, as it mentions in this document? You were there, as I recall from your testimony yesterday.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993 -- I do not recall this detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't ever recall Colonel Blagojevic coming over to Bratunac and being a deputy commander, your deputy commander, chief of staff for a while?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where was Colonel Blagojevic before he became commander of the brigade in -- you may recall he became commander of the Bratunac Brigade on 25 May 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was with the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his position there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was in the operations sector -- no, sorry. No, no, no. He was at the head -- or the chief of engineering corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you're aware that there was a corps engineering battalion at Konjevic Polje, the 5th Engineering Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so, as chief of engineers of the Drina Corps, Colonel Blagojevic would have dealt with and made recommendations regarding the use of the 5th Engineering Battalion at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long Colonel Blagojevic was the chief of engineers at the corps before becoming commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea? Two years? One year? Just a couple of weeks?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Calls for speculation. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. The witness has answered that he has no idea about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we've heard in this courtroom that in late May/early June the Bratunac Brigade was involved in a -- some sort of an attack or mock attack on the UN checkpoint at Zeleni Jadar, and that as a result of that attack, that checkpoint was withdrawn by the UN. It was something I believe was referred to as Operation Jadar. Now, such an operation would have taken logistic support, I imagine. Do you recall this operation in the Zeleni Jadar area late May/early June?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not recall it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You inventoried -- or we saw an inventory of the UN OPs after the fall of Srebrenica. Do you remember inventorying the materiels left behind at the UN/Zeleni Jadar checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that assumes that there was an inventory of anything that was captured after. So perhaps if we could have a predicate. Perhaps there is a document that would demonstrate that they captured materiel that needed to be inventoried, as we have, for instance, after the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In cross-examination that's not necessary, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a perfectly clear question, did he inventory materiel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we saw documents of the inventory of the UN left over in Srebrenica, but we are not sure whether that inventory listed some equipment left behind in that Zeleni Jadar checkpoint. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: My question is not related to that, Your Honour. I just want to know if they inventoried any property from the Zeleni Jadar checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may try. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inventory any property from the Zeleni Jadar checkpoint in June 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've also heard that some of the battalions were required to send men down to the Zeleni Jadar area prior to the attack on Srebrenica. I take it those -- to help fill the line and take up some of the space that was created there when the UN checkpoint was left. Did you supply any logistics for those men that were moving down to Zeleni Jadar prior to the attack on the enclave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you have told us -- if I could just briefly now refer to the Krivaja 95 attack plan, the corps plan, which is Exhibit 543. And just, I think, for convenience, there's also the attack plan with Mr. -- Colonel Blagojevic's name at the bottom of it, citing this other one. If we could get that document as well. That's a Defence exhibit, I believe. So did you -- I believe you testified you had a chance to know about this Drina Corps attack plan. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- were you actually able to read it at some point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was informed -- I familiarised myself, rather, with item 9, the logistics. I was not interested in the other particulars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was it in fact read out to you at some point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just note in the minutes of the brigade command of 5 July, it notes that the brigade commander presented the order of the Drina Corps command. Do you remember that the day before the attack, that Blagojevic presented this order to the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Colonel Blagojevic would have been fully familiar with this order, Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that this plan did not envision actually taking the enclave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that there were two principal objectives to this plan? One was to separate the enclaves of Zepa, Srebrenica, stop the infiltration between the two. Are you aware of that objective?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you also aware of the objective to -- on the -- during the attack of the Srebrenica enclave, that the objective was to reduce the enclave to the urban area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so if you knew that, Colonel Blagojevic would have been aware of that object as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the city area or the urban area of Srebrenica, about how big is that? We know it's kind of a long -- or it's a skinny, narrow city, but can you just give us roughly what dimensions it would be.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the area? The width, the length, the area? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. Just the width of the town and the length of the town, of the actual urban area.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is approximately as regards the length from the sports stadium to the exit from Srebrenica towards Jadar, where there is a bakery, this is about 4 kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four kilometres by about how wide?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about a kilometre, a kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that at the time of the attack on Srebrenica, a good large number of the Muslim population of the enclave lived outside the urban area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were informed that the bulk of the population was there, in Srebrenica, immediately in Srebrenica proper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know about the Swedish shelter project, where thousands of Muslims lived outside of Srebrenica? You may have inventoried some of the many materiels from that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we heard about this settlement in the Jadar valley. I cannot recall its name. If that is the Swedish project you are referring to, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday when you were, I believe, speaking of the Krivaja 95 document and I believe Colonel Blagojevic's document, you had mentioned you believed that a reference in, I believe it was the Blagojevic document, was a reference to the Drina Corps Krivaja 95 document. And just to try to remind you, the reference was to a document that was dated -- numbered 156-1. And Mr. Karnavas pointed out to you that the Krivaja 95 Drina Corps document was 156-2. And you had testified you thought, well -- that it was the same document. Well, we have found a document of that same date dated 156-1. And just to clear this up to make sure we've got the documents straight, I wanted to show you this document 156-1, which is also dated 2 July, and it's directed -- signed off by General Zivanovic, the corps commander, and it is directed to the subordinate units of the Drina Corps. And it's basically a call to arms to get ready and to get troops together for the upcoming offensive activities, which are to begin 4 July. And so if you could just take a look at that. Would this be the correct document, the one that was referenced in the Blagojevic document? It's 862/A, for the record.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see a thing here. It's a poor copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise about that. And in any event, I don't think there will be any objection, so we will try to get a better copy for the record. Now, you talked a little bit about Pribicevac. Can you describe the command area of Pribicevac. It's basically a tiny little village on a hillside, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many buildings were there at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very few; maybe a couple.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One was used as a command centre for the corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the command of the 3rd Battalion, and I don't know whether the corps command ever used it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But there weren't very many buildings there is fair enough to say, I guess.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've described briefly your position and the people, the few people that you -- your assistants under you, and you've given us their names. Did you have any more immediate staff besides I think those three people?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a rear company, a logistics company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had a whole rear service company that you were responsible for?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, Colonel Blagojevic bore overall responsibility of that rear service company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire brigade, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe how many men were in the rear service company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just briefly describe to us the, you know, the hierarchy there. Who was in command of the rear service company and what kind of staff did that person have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The company commander was Captain Radosavljevic. He had a technical staff -- quartermaster staff and transport staff, or squad. And he was their immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was this company located?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the centre of town, in the vicinity of the medical centre there. It was an old building that used to be used by the Territorial Defence and the agriculture cooperative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were active and on duty on 12 and 13 July, this company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, save for Captain Radosavljevic, who was off duty at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So who was in charge in his absence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, squad commanders had their duties, and they would perform them according to their given tasks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, somebody must have been in charge of the company when the commander was absent.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had an assistant whose name I can't remember at the moment. He had an assistant; however, his job was not that difficult at worst of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that from the corps there was Colonel Acamovic and I believe it was a Lieutenant Colonel Krsmanovic from the rear services of the corps. What other staff or soldiers, if any, were there in Bratunac on the 12th, 13th, or 14th from the corps, rear services?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you all of their names; however, people would come, deliver materiel and equipment, fuel. I personally didn't see them and I was not supposed to see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how many corps people were there besides these two officers? Rear service types I mean.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- but there was a large group of the Bratunac Brigade that was able to do their rear service, logistics support, transportation, quartermaster job at the time. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We performed our regular tasks, which consisted in supplying our own brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you assist the corps in the operation to help transport the Muslims out of Potocari? For example, did you help with the fuel, the counting of the fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from the rear services company did give a hand with everything that was needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was their job, wasn't it, to work together with the corps to get the job done, to get all those people moved out to Kladanj, where they could be looked after?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People from the rear services company were not together with the corps personnel. From time to time, there would be a task which required additional assistance, and that's when we would be called in to provide that additional assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from time to time you did provide additional assistance to the corps in the movement of the Muslim population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no special need for us to do that. The corps had its own organisation, and there was nothing for us to do there, nothing special for us to do there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I think you've said you provided two buses on the 12th of July to help transport the Muslims. Is that true what you said yesterday? Did you provide two buses that had been mobilised by the Bratunac Brigade to help transport the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an order to do that -- to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure there was orders to do all of this, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, there was an order for the buses to be provided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the situation for these two buses, you assisted the corps in the job to get the Muslims moved out to Kladanj, as you were ordered.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what Mladic promised to the Muslims, and for us it was an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the answer is: You did assist the corps and the Main Staff in moving the Muslims out with these two buses. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of July, but not later than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's stay with the 12th for now. You also were shown a lot of documents, and I don't really want to go over them, these fuel documents, many of which were written in handwriting that you recognised. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did recognise them. They are reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so in respect to accounting for the fuel used in the transportation operation, the Bratunac Brigade played a significant role in accounting for this valuable fuel that was used in the operation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to clarify this. Yesterday I said that we had tried --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could answer the question and then you can clarify --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, objection Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The gentleman is trying to answer the question and he's being interrupted, rudely I might add, by the Prosecutor. He's entitled to give his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you may go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was objecting to his answer as non-responsive because there's nothing to clarify. I need an answer before he can clarify. I would like a clarification, that's fine; but you can't clarify a non-answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe the witness did not understand your question quite well. Let's hear the clarification from this witness first. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday I said that we had accounted for the entry and exit of fuel, which doesn't imply that this fuel was used, for example, for the transport of Muslims. The paperwork accounting for the entry and exit of the fuel was what was asked from us to do, and this is exactly what we did, the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But in any major operation that involves fuel, accounting for that fuel is an important part of the overall operation, isn't it, so the command knows how it was used, what was used, what wasn't used, that none was stolen? Isn't the accounting an important part of any operation, business, military, or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accounting is important in any case, because it justifies the use of all the materiel and equipment. And from day one, our paperwork and our accounting was in order in our brigade because it was our obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. And we also saw that the accounting documents were dated 12 and 13 July, when all this was going on. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 12th of July, the Muslim population was gathered in Potocari; it's a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people that were doing the accounting, I believe including yourself, were on the ground at the time the fuel was being accepted, delivered, passed out, so they were on the ground working and doing the accounting at the time of the events. This wasn't some after-the-fact post-accounting, looking over records. Your accounting was done from the ground, where this activity was happening, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that the fuel at the Vihor was dispensed by Vihor staff in the Vihor parking lot at the entrance to Bratunac. And also, the drivers from the corps were involved in that fueling operation. And then, based on what they did, we recorded the fuel that was filled into vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you know that because you were on the ground observing that and accounting for it. Either you or your staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure I wasn't there. My assistant was informed, but he did not need to be present. He was just provided with the paperwork that would justify his subsequent accounting, and that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you talked a little bit yesterday about a statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor back in 26 November 2001. Thank you. And you've had a chance to go over that document because the Defence showed it to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that interview, did you try to be as truthful and as correct as possible?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you've pointed out one thing, which I'll get into later, that you have changed. You admitted that you told the Office of the Prosecutor that Mr. Blagojevic was in Potocari on the 12th, but you've now testified that you were wrong on that point. Is that right? I'll get into that a little bit later, but is there anything else that you want to change of significance in your statement besides that point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness come closer to the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The interpreters are having a little bit of a hard time hearing you. If you could move your chair up a little bit, they've asked, so you're a little closer to the mike. Thank you. Make yourself comfortable, but this won't be too long. We're not going to be here all day, I hope.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could provide the witness with a B/C/S copy of his statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to just go over some of the things you said, and I'll direct you to certain parts of the statement. I -- we've tried to highlight some of them, but don't -- you don't need to limit yourself to the highlighting, you can, of course, look above or beyond to help understand the context of it. Those highlights are just meant to attract your attention. Now, the first part I want to ask you about is -- it's page 12 of the English and lines 13 through 19. And yours should be page 12, lines 7 through 13. And the question is asked: "Okay. The next thing you heard about the evacuation or removal?" And you say: "So in all those activities there were the rear services organs of the corps that were doing their job. So for that part of the operation, the assistant commander for the rear service on the corps level would ask me, request from me something that he maybe did not have at the time and I did have. The fact is that we provided a certain number - I cannot recall exactly how many - a certain number of buses and trucks for transportation of people." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's fine, but is that a true statement, first of all? And you can always clarify any answer you give.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement is probably correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Probably? Only probably?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain. I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the brigade we didn't have more than two buses or trucks. When I said "we," I probably meant Bratunac, the buses that belonged to Vihor as well as the lorries that belonged to Vihor which were mobilised by the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I think we'll get into that a little later, so let's go on to the next section. And that should be, in the English, page 14, and it should be for you page 14 lines 24 through 26. For us it should be about lines 17 through 24. And you're talking about buses and trucks. And the investigator asked you: "And where would you have got those buses and trucks from?" And you say: "In the brigade we had two buses and the rest we took from the transportation company Vihor." And I think that's what you testified to yesterday, that there were two buses in the brigade and that the other vehicles you took from Vihor and provided for this operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "we," I was probably referring to the Army of Republika Srpska. I put myself in that role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I can read to you what you said. You said: "In the brigade, we had two buses." So you're not talking in the VRS; you're talking in the brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not entitled to that. We were -- we didn't have the right to take any buses from Vihor ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, they got mobilised.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were involved in that, getting the buses -- or the -- it says: "The rest we took from the transportation company Vihor." And you've just referred to the Bratunac Brigade, so it's you -- it's the brigade and the corps getting these vehicles from Vihor, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the corps that mobilised those buses pursuant to their own request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you say "we," you're referring to the Drina Corps, even though you're not -- you're a brigade guy. You know, that doesn't make any sense. Can you explain that? That's all right. We can go on. If you could be shown what's been marked as D161. This is something I -- it's a document that was shown to you yesterday, and I'm hoping you have a better photocopy of the B/C/S version. Because we can see on English that there's a little note on the bottom that says: "In the original, items 18, 19, 20, 21, and 22 are connected with a curve brace above which stands: Vihor, 13 July." Now, in the copy that unfortunately was used yesterday, that was hard to see. And we've got the original document that if I could show you that I think it would be most helpful. So first of all, looking at that original document, do you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was found in the Bratunac Brigade during the search in 1998.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise it -- actually, these are two different handwritings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, I think you're right. And if you could look from 18 to 22, do you see that little -- that mark? And it says: "Vihor." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, these are three different handwritings. The upper part, the black ink, is one handwriting; the second one is from 14 to 17; and the third one is from 18 to 22. Yes, I can see the marking "Vihor" and the date. I suppose this fuel was filled in the Vihor company, and somebody must have added this on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, and you -- as I just read over your statement, you said: "We had two buses and the rest we took from the transportation company Vihor." Would these five entries be the buses or vehicles that were taken from Vihor?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we didn't take them, that it was the corps that took them. But these are not buses. It says here "TAM 130, FAP 1616," and those are not buses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I thank you for clarifying that. You're correct. I should not have said buses. Okay. Let's go to another section, and it's page 15 on the English. And it should be page 15 on yours as well. I'm sorry, I don't have an actual line number. And Mr. Manning, the investigator, asked you: "What about" -- line 3: "What about fuel for those vehicles?" And you say: "The fuel was provided from the corps and all other materiel was provided by the corps." And the investigator says: "Did the UNPROFOR provide fuel as well?" And you say: "Yes, some. Yes, I cannot tell you how much, which part UNPROFOR provided in total. But the DutchBat soldiers gave us one tanker, one cistern with fuel." The investigator says: "Did they give it to you personally, your troops personally?" And you say: "Yes, the brigade. Our brigade took that fuel. We dumped the fuel in the cistern of the tanker truck of the transportation Vihor company." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained yesterday: Colonel Acamovic asked from me to find a solution for this huge quantity of fuel. It was my suggestion, and this is what was indeed done, to dump all that fuel in the tanks of the Vihor company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And the Bratunac Brigade did that, working with the corps, according to your statement. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Acamovic asked me to do it, and I obeyed. I did it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did he ask or order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A superior officer issues orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So this is a true statement that I just read?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With the qualifications of the explanations that he just gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could sense that by ourself, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But -- yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what I said -- what you said, excuse me, to us in Banja Luka was correct, and you're adding to it today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Manning, the investigator, put pressure on me, and I felt very uncomfortable at the moment. I did not have the opportunity to explain all the details. The essence of the matter is that the fuel was secured by Colonel Acamovic through Dutch -- through the DutchBat. And he asked me to find a solution for storing this huge quantity of fuel, and I found a solution. This is what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said: "Our brigade took that fuel. We dumped the fuel in the cistern of the tanker truck of the transportation company Vihor." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said already, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go now to the English page 17. And for you it should be page 18, about lines 5 through 8. And Mr. Manning says: "I don't know whether it's simply a misunderstanding, but I'm asking you, the transportation of people - and it's obvious to both of us who we're speaking of - but I want you to tell me." And you say: "Okay. So the fuel was used for the combat activities around Srebrenica and the transportation of the people that I mentioned earlier; women, children, and elderly." Mr. Manning says: "The Muslim population of Srebrenica and Potocari?" And you say: "Yes." Is that correct, a true statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What fuel are you referring to? The 30 tonnes of fuel. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think you're -- that's what's mentioned above. You're talking about, as far as I can tell, and you can correct me if I'm wrong, but the fuel that you got from UNPROFOR and put into the Vihor cistern.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't mean to object but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- for proper context perhaps we could go a page earlier and let the gentleman at least for his own purposes before answering any questions, starting perhaps as early as line 22, page 16, on the English version, where the document with the ERN number of 0067-1769 is presented to him. And perhaps -- that was on page 16. It would be page 16, I believe line 24, on the Srpski version. And then he could just -- because I think we are losing some context, because it talks about the 30 plus the 52.000 litres. So I think in all fairness to the witness, he should be given an opportunity to read that entire section so he can make sure that he gives us a full and complete and honest answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President -- I'm sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that at the very beginning of the cross-examination on this statement, the Prosecution already said that the witness could read certain pages and consider the question in the context of the whole statement. But thank you very much to point out that place. Witness, you have the statement at your hand. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You could read the specific pages the Defence counsel pointed out and then answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was giving this statement, I had no idea -- namely, I had data on the consumed quantities. I had no idea where it had been consumed and in which way. Only after I had familiarised myself with the documentation, I realised that the fuel had not been actually consumed but was just accounted for, had been actually passed through our documentation. Obviously, this fuel which we received from the Dutch Battalion could not have been spent for combat operations around Srebrenica, because the combat operations ended on the 11th. It could have been used to transport Muslims, and it was actually received for that purpose, as far as I gathered from Colonel Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And I think you've said that someplace before, that this fuel was received to transport the Muslims, and you tell us in this statement that at least some of it was in fact used to transport the Muslims. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This fuel we did -- we received from the Dutch Battalion. We got it from them in order to transport the Muslims; that is clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go -- if we could go to page 18 in the English. It should be page 18, lines 18 to 20 for you in the B/C/S. Mr. Manning asked: "How could you have gotten fuel from Vihor, Gradina, and the Bratunac municipality? What is the mechanisms?" And you say: "Considering that the corps could not provide enough quantities of fuel or food for the brigade, not only during that period but also earlier, so we as a brigade asked for the assistance from the companies and from the municipality so the quantities of fuel, food, cigarettes that we were lacking in the brigade that the corps could not provide for us, we received from the companies in Bratunac." Is that a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this way, we obtained provisions of food and fuel for the regular activities for the life and work of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the brigade had the ability to go to the municipality and get materiel on a normal basis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We go down the page a little bit and Mr. Manning says: "You were able to provide some buses and trucks and fuel for the transportation of the civilians. Who drove the trucks and buses that you provided?" And you say: "So not all the buses and trucks we provided. The corps also provided buses and trucks." That's correct. That's basically what you have been telling us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then Mr. Manning says: "The ones that you provided." And you say: "Yes." And Mr. Manning says: "Who drove them?" And you say: "The drivers from Vihor company, from the transportation company." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buses and the trucks that had been mobilised from Vihor to transport the Muslims were -- was only logical they should be driven by Vihor's drivers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's a true statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that these buses and trucks which had been mobilised were driven by Vihor drivers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the next question is: "And the buses and trucks that were provided by the brigade, who drove those?" And you say: "We had our drivers." And Mr. Manning says: "And they would be from which section of the brigade?" And you say: "The rear service company of the brigade." So the buses -- the two buses that have been spoken of earlier, the people that drove those buses, were they from the rear services company of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buses that had been mobilised, the two buses in the brigade were driven by drivers belonging to the rear services company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. If you could now go to page 20. It's page 20 in the English as well. Lines 21 through 24 in the B/C/S. And around 10 through 16. Mr. Manning is asking you about: "What else did you do that day?" You say: "I can't tell precisely what else I could have done that day." And Mr. Manning says: "Did you -- you explained to me that you had some dealings with your commander on the 12th. When was the last time you saw him on the 12th and where?" And you say: "It's been a long time ago. I can't remember. It's very difficult just to remember one particular day. We were in contact all day, but we were not all the time together. But from the morning until the evening, we were all the time in contact. And one was at one duty and the other was at another duty." So this says that you were in contact all day with Colonel Blagojevic. Not personal contact, but -- is that true?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I mean by contact is that we talked on the telephone. If the need arose, we were there in the command; and if the need arose, we would get in touch in this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this says that you were actually in contact with him, either by the phone or personally, all day. And we know this was a very busy day and it would have been normal for the rear services officer to be in close contact with his commander during this day. So my question is: Were you in contact with him off and on all day, either by phone or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again, if the gentleman could be given some time. I know that he was advised and told that he could look at it, but the questions are coming like this. The gentleman could be given some time so he could read from 20 all the way to 22, at least all the way -- yeah, to 22, end of 22, be given time, because I believe he's asked a series of questions with respect to that, so we can have a more complete answer. In the event that he's not given that opportunity, I want to make it abundantly clear through re-direct examination I'm going to go through each and every line where I believe more context should be placed in these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you could raise your objections, but don't make any gestures, especially to make some sounds out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware I was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is a courtroom, not a coffee stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't aware, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course the witness has the opportunity to read this statement, but it's time for a break, Mr. McCloskey. We might have a break now and during the break I hope the witness could take advantage of that time and read the statement. Is that all right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, did you read your statement during the break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to answer the question? Or, Mr. McCloskey, you may repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was the area that we talked about on page 20, your lines 21 through, roughly, 24. And English page 20, 13 through 16. Where you say: "It's difficult to remember one particular day, but we were in contact all day but we were not all the time together. But from the morning to the evening, we were all the time in contact. And one was at one duty and the other was at the other duty." So is that a fair and truthful statement that you made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And on the same subject, it's page 28 about 11 through 16 on the English. It's around 13 through 15 in the B/C/S. And Mr. Manning says: "Okay. A simple question of communication. Did your commander have a portable radio, a Motorola or similar?" And you say: "Yes, he probably did." Mr. Manning says: "And if necessary, you could contact him on the radio or telephone or some other means during that period?" And you say: "Yes, yes." So the period we are talking about, is that a true statement for July 12 and 13, that you could contact him if you needed to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I clarify this for the benefit of the Prosecutor. On all these pages, from 20 to 28, he insisted for me to say that I was with the commander; I never confirmed this. I just said it was a possibility for us to get in touch via the communication means if the need arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, there is no misunderstanding on that point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So like you say here, you're able to get a hold of him when you needed him during those days, 12 and 13?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go on to another subject. And this is about what you tell us about what you see when you're in Potocari. And if we could start with page 29, 14 -- line about 14 in the English. Oddly enough, it's about the same line in the B/C/S. And I'll just read it. Mr. Manning says: "Okay. When you were in Potocari on the 12th, you saw the Muslim civilians. Who was guarding those people? Who was providing security for those people, apart from DutchBat?" And you say: "Our police." And Mr. Manning says: "What police? Military police? Civilian police? Special police?" And you say: "Mostly military police. Military police. Brigade had its police and the corps had their own police." And Mr. Manning says: "And do I take it from that that it was Bratunac Brigade military police?" And you say: "Both, Bratunac Brigade and the corps." So when you were in Potocari, did you see both the Bratunac Brigade military police and the corps military police, like you say here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were providing security for the Muslims, like you say here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page 30. English it should be starting about line 4. It should be about line 5 -- roughly line 5 in the B/C/S. Mr. Manning says: "But which ones did you recognise from that day?" And you say: "They were all there that day. The majority of them were there. That was their main task. Maybe the duty officer remained at the brigade, but ..." And Mr. Manning says: "Okay. At some stage the men that did remain in Potocari were separated from the women and children. Are you aware of that?" And you say: "No." Before I get to that separation question, maybe you should look a little bit between my last thing I read to you and that first one so we can tell what unit we're talking about. And Mr. Manning says: "But which ones did you recognise from that day?" As you can see on page 29, one of the things Mr. Manning says is: "Taking back to the crowd of people, the bread, the incidents, the Bratunac Brigade military police are there, you would have seen some of the Bratunac military police you recognise. You lived there all your life. Who did you recognise?" "We met everyone, so it's irrelevant whether I met. I cannot tell you whether I met that military policeman there or I met him in Bratunac or I met him somewhere else. It's difficult. You see those people every day." And then he says: "But which ones did you recognise from that day?" And you say: "They were all there that day. The majority of them were there. That was their main task. Maybe the duty officer remained at the brigade, but ..." So you're telling Mr. Manning there that the majority of the Bratunac Brigade military police were in Potocari that day, on the 12th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bratunac police, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Bratunac Brigade military police. Is that what you're talking -- that's what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you stand by this statement that the majority of the -- you saw the majority of the Bratunac Brigade military police in Potocari on 12 July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should just like to say this: Item 6 -- well, probably all of them were there. Most of them, the majority was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's true. The majority -- you believe the majority of them were there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know there were about 33 Bratunac Brigade military police on the roster of July 1995? Does that sound about right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's now go to page 30, lines 1 through 6. And it's -- on yours it should be page 31, lines 11 through 18.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where is this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Actually, it's -- should be -- I'm sorry. I gave you the wrong page. It should be -- it's page 30, lines 5 through 10. Sorry. That's the one we've already gone over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to page 33, and it should be page 33, line 8 for you, and it's line 7 for us. And you just say: "The military police were there for sure." So there's no doubt in your mind that the Bratunac Brigade military police were there on that date. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next reference I want to go to is -- it should be page 50 on yours, lines -- around 2 to 11. On the English it's page 52. But let's start at -- I guess at about line 4. Mr. Manning says: "And who was directing them to do this? Who was directing where the vehicles to go?" And you say: "I don't know about that. Unofficially, I don't know. I mean, I heard, but I think it is a misunderstanding in translation. I heard that they were supposed to go to Kladanj, and that's what I -- that was the separation line where we could drop them, the Muslims, so they could go towards Tuzla." Mr. Manning says: "But you said before that the police would be directing the buses where to park and where to turn." And you say: "Yes." And Mr. Manning says: "And you saw that happening?" And you say: "Yes." And Mr. Manning says: "What sort of police were they?" And you say: "Our military police." And Mr. Manning says: "By 'our' you mean Bratunac Brigade?" And you say: "Yes." So simply, you're telling Mr. Manning that you saw the Bratunac Brigade military police directing the buses where to park and where to turn. So is that true? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you also told Mr. Manning that you saw the protection -- soldiers from the Protection Regiment in Potocari that day. Do you recall seeing the -- any Protection Regiment soldiers in Potocari on the 12th? I can point it out if you want to help -- your recollection refreshed.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want to help me with the page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 35, line 20 to 22.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you see soldiers from the Protection Regiment in Potocari on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said it was something like the 65th paratroopers or something like that. You remember the number 65 as the designation for that Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Dean Manning who mentioned the 65 Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. He mentioned it first, and then you said: "I'm not sure. We just called them simply Protection Regiment. That sounds like something 65th paratroopers in Serbia, maybe you mixed it up." So does the 65 ring any bells at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Protection Regiment you're talking about, you say that it's a Main Staff unit. Right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they have a base that was located near Bratunac? Konjevic Polje/Nova Kasaba area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they were in Nova Kasaba. I can't remember exactly, but it does ring a bell, Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to ask you about something you said yesterday when you were testifying about what you saw in Potocari. And I've got on page 53 of your testimony Mr. Karnavas asked you: "Now, did you see any members of the Bratunac Brigade there, whether they were soldiers or military police?" And your answer was: "There were members of the Bratunac Brigade there." And the question was: "Okay. Do you recall what they were doing, if anything?" And you said: "Well, at that moment they were providing security. They were engaged in separating soldiers from the Muslim population." What did you mean when you said: "They were engaged in separating soldiers from the Muslim population"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it here in the statement, but I can explain, however, no problem. I can clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just explain. I'm sorry. I'm going from yesterday's testimony, not from what you told us in Banja Luka. So you can just put that aside.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then, you mentioned page 53. I've been looking for it. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I was directing the other folks to the trial transcript. I should have been clear. So can you tell us what you meant when you said: "They were engaged in separating soldiers from the Muslim population."

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I said: The DutchBat was engaged in the separation and so were our police. All of us who were there at the moment, including myself, who was one of the soldiers, we wanted to prevent people from crossing a certain line that was set.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we know that the Dutch strung a big -- some kind of tape that separated the population from some of the VRS soldiers and some of the Dutch soldiers. Is that the separation you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The DutchBat soldiers did put this band. There were a lot of us there, soldiers, officers, people who were just curious. And the military police had a task to preserve order, to provide security, to provide security for that operation that was underway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. Did you see able-bodied Muslim men separated from their families as their families were being loaded on buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you said you were separating soldiers from the Muslim population, you meant separating Dutch soldiers, VRS soldiers from the big Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the police was there to look after the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, the military police of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any military-aged or able-bodied Muslim men amongst the big crowd of people in Potocari while you were there during that hour or hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were mostly elderly people, women, and children. I didn't see able-bodied men among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were there for an hour and a half, in that area among the people, roughly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not among the people, not in the crowd. I was on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had a good look at the people on the other side of the tape?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw some people being loaded onto buses and trucks from that crowd?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Women, children, the elderly were walking towards the buses in some sort of a column.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have heard horrendous evidence that at that time male members, able-bodied members, were taken away from their families --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. We've heard no evidence that anybody was taken away when General Mladic was there. The gentleman testified that when he was there, General Mladic was there. I would like to see any footage or any transcript that shows that when General Mladic was there, the males were being separated. That occurred much later. So the possibility exists that while he was there none of that was happening. And I think if -- we can go over this over and over and over --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's a very fine argument and if he wants to make it, that's fine. Why he needs to make it in front of the witness is beyond me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I don't think the Prosecution has finished his question yet. Maybe he will set a time frame there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He hasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, he hasn't finished his question yet, from the transcript, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: We've heard some horrendous evidence that at the time on 12 July in the afternoon, male members of the family, able-bodied men, were separated from their families, to the horror and misery of their families. Did you see any of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you are telling me what you've heard. I myself didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all I was asking. Okay. Let's go to page -- we can go back to the book that I originally gave you just briefly. And if you could go to page 34, about lines 17 through 22. A person named Mark Vlasic that was in the interview. This is on line 18 of page 34 of the English. "You mentioned that Blagojevic was in Potocari on the 12th. In fact, he was there with you when you were there." And you say: "That's what I said." And Mr. Vlasic says: "Okay. So while you were there, Blagojevic was there. Both of you saw the military police who were there?" And you say: "Yes." You've had a chance to read this. Does this accurately reflect what you told Mr. Vlasic that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking right now whether the substance of it is correct, but is that in fact what you said? You see the B/C/S words written down there. Do you have any reason to think you didn't say those words?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said that I made a mistake, and I apologise to Mr. Blagojevic for the mistake that I made. I was put in a situation where I succumbed to the pressure and I said this, but it's simply not correct. I did not see Colonel Blagojevic there on the 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did in fact tell us that, as it states in this document. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've said that I made a mistake. My answer was wrong and I don't see a problem here at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us then that you were with him in Potocari. Not just that you saw him there but you were with him there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Potocari with Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that's what you're saying now, but you told us you were with him in Potocari, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, this has been asked and answered. I don't object. I just hope that the Court will give me the latitude and demonstrate the patience it is demonstrating right now as we go over these questions over and over again, because I think that he's answered the question. Now, if he's going to ask the questions over and over again, I would like sufficient latitude on re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I think anyway the witness has answered that question. Or if not, the implication is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, he answered the question that he told us he saw Blagojevic in Potocari. He has not answered the question whether or not he told us that he was with Blagojevic in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I understand that. But he said that he's wrong. The precondition is that he told you about that in the previous interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Of course I want the Trial Chamber to understand what he told us, but I think that's clear. So I won't go with it any further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, after telling us that Mr. Blagojevic was in Potocari, did you make any effort to contact us to correct that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not send me a copy of my statement, although I requested that via Mr. Trivun Jovicic. I don't know what his position is. I never received a copy of my statement, although I did ask for one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jovicic is the Republika Srpska liaison officer to this Tribunal, and we never received your request that I'm aware of. And if we did, then we failed to provide it. But my question is: Did you ever make an effort to inform us that you had made a mistake when putting Mr. Blagojevic in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of having said that. This interview lasted a whole day, and I just couldn't remember what I said. For example, last year in April Mr. Trivun Jovicic asked me to give another statement. Since I am entitled to receive a copy of my first statement, Mr. Jovicic promised I would get that, but he never contacted me again. I really wanted to see what I had said during the nine hours of the interview that I gave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you made that statement to us, did you have a chance to talk to Mr. Blagojevic on the telephone or in some other way about the statement you had given to us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't remember when Mr. Blagojevic was arrested, and this statement I gave on the 26th. And I really can't remember whether Colonel Blagojevic had been at large at the time. If this happened after he was arrested, my statement I mean, then obviously I couldn't contact him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When was the first time you told anyone that Mr. Blagojevic was not at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember who was it that I said that to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you say it to Defence counsel, which is perfectly appropriate, in preparing for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I spoke with my associates and when I looked at the TV footage, I realised that I didn't see Colonel Blagojevic there. And this was confirmed to me by my associates. And they told me that Mr. Blagojevic just wasn't there, that he was in the command. And then it was that I realised that I actually hadn't seen him in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were these associates that told you he wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My associates told me that he was in the brigade command. This is what I had just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But who were the associates? What people told you this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example Milomir Stanojevic, Dragan Josipovic, his associate in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you interviewed with us, did you think you were on video?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see myself on video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you think you were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Manning showed me a video footage in Banja Luka. I could see a lot of officers. And then I realised that I couldn't see Blagojevic. However, this statement was given under pressure. I gave in to the pressure, and I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you think you were on video when you answered Mr. Manning's questions? Did you think you were on video in Potocari on the 12th of July when you answered his questions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't think that. I didn't even know how much of the video footage there was. I didn't know who was filming the situation, and I just was shown some of it. I believe that soldiers of the DutchBat also had cameras and they were filming. Whether they did it officially or whether they did it with their own private cameras, I don't know. In any case, they were filming what was going on at this what I called separation line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you felt there was a whole lot of film of Potocari that you hadn't seen during -- when you were -- when you gave us that statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, going over to the 13th, we've seen some documents relating to the accounting of the fuel. I won't go over those. You've told us the two Bratunac Brigade buses were pulled out of the Muslim transportation operation and provided for the chief of staff and his folks to go towards Bracan. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did those two buses come back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the huge convoy of buses and trucks that was lined up in the middle of town in Bratunac on the morning of the 14th of July, the day after the last Muslims were transported out of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were convoys on the 12th and on the 13th. I'm not sure about the 14th, but if this is what you say, then okay. But I'm not sure. On those days, there were a lot of buses. The whole thing started on the 12th, continued through the 13th. Whether any of them were left there on the 14th, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't want you to take my word for it. I want you to go back to your memory. You've told us you were in and around the command and this area during this time period. You were around on the 14th, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was around. I was around, but I can't remember all the dates. For example, sending people to the area of Bracani was a simple task. The commander was given an order to inform me, I informed my associates what needed to be done, and the procedure was simple: Buses, food, and the rest, and I just left it at that. And it was their job to carry the order through. And that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night on the 13th of July, that second day that the Muslim population was transported out of Potocari, in fact the day that it was finished that evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my own apartment, in the centre of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How close to the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across the road from it, some 50 metres from it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what direction?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by the direction?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: North? South? East? West? South-west? North-east?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC [Resumed]
